readings.title: The Trespass of Intermingling
readings.subtitle: Compromising the Set-Apart Seed with Systemic Corruption
readings.text: [Ezra 9:1] And when these matters had been done, the leaders came to me, saying, “The people of Yisra’ěl and the priests and the Lěvites have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands, as to their abominations, those of the Kena‛anites, the Ḥittites, the Perizzites, the Yeḇusites, the Ammonites, the Mo’aḇites, the Mitsrites, and the Amorites, [2] for they have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and their sons, so that the set-apart seed is intermingled with the peoples of those lands. And the hand of the leaders and rulers has been foremost in this trespass.”

readings.title: The Weight of the Transgression
readings.subtitle: Gathering the Remnant Who Tremble at the Word
readings.text: [Ezra 9:3] And when I heard this word, I tore my garment and my robe, and plucked out some of the hair of my head and beard, and sat down astonished. [4] Then all those who trembled at the words of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl gathered to me, because of the trespass of the exiles, and I sat astonished until the evening offering.

readings.title: The Posture of Affliction
readings.subtitle: Confessing the Generational Guilt and Ruin
readings.text: [Ezra 9:5] And at the evening offering I rose from my affliction. And having torn my garment and my robe, I fell on my knees and spread out my hands to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, [6] and said, “O my <dn>Elohim</dn>, I am too ashamed and wounded to lift up <dn>את</dn> my face to You, my <dn>Elohim</dn>, for our crookednesses have risen higher than our heads, and our guilt has grown up to the heavens. [7] “Since the days of our fathers to this day we have been very guilty, and for our crookednesses we, our sovereigns, and our priests have been given into the hand of the sovereigns of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, and to plunder, and to shame of faces, as it is this day.

readings.title: The Grace of the Remnant
readings.subtitle: A Peg in the Set-Apart Place and Reviving in Bondage
readings.text: [Ezra 9:8] “But now, for a short while, favour has been shown from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, to leave us a remnant to escape, and to give us a peg in <dn>His</dn> set-apart place, that our <dn>Elohim</dn> might enlighten our eyes and give us a little reviving in our bondage. [9] “For we were slaves, but in our bondage our <dn>Elohim</dn> did not forsake us, and extended loving-commitment to us in the presence of the sovereigns of Persia, to revive us, to raise up <dn>את</dn> the House of our <dn>Elohim</dn>, to restore its ruins, and to give us a wall in Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim.

readings.title: The Warning of Uncleanness
readings.subtitle: The Failure to Maintain a Tahor Jurisdiction
readings.text: [Ezra 9:10] “And now, O our <dn>Elohim</dn>, what do we say after this? For we have forsaken Your commands, [11] which You have commanded by <dn>את</dn> Your servants the prophets, saying, ‘The land which you are going in to possess is a land unclean through the uncleanness of the peoples of the lands, by their abominations with which they have filled it, from one end to another, by their uncleanness. [12] And now, do not give <dn>את</dn> your daughters as wives for their sons, nor take <dn>את</dn> their daughters to your sons. And do not seek <dn>את</dn> their peace or <dn>את</dn> wealth ever, so that you are strong, and shall eat the good of the land, and leave it as an inheritance to your children forever.’

readings.title: The Righteousness of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: Appealing to the Creator's Unmerited Deliverance
readings.text: [Ezra 9:13] “And after all that has come upon us for our evil deeds and for our great guilt, since You our <dn>Elohim</dn> have held back the rod upon our crookednesses, and have given us such deliverance as this, [14] should we turn back, to break Your commands, and join in marriage with the people of these abominations? Would You not be enraged with us until You had consumed us, so that there would be no remnant or survivor? [15] “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, You are righteous, for we are left as a remnant, as it is this day. See, we are before You, in our guilt, for there is no one to stand before You concerning this!”

readings.title: The Covenant of Restoration
readings.subtitle: Severing Ties with the Adversary's System
readings.text: [Ezra 10:1] And while Ezra was praying, and while he was confessing, weeping, and bowing down before the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>, a very large assembly – men and women and children – gathered unto him from Yisra’ěl, for the people wept very bitterly. [2] And Sheḵanyah son of Yeḥi’ěl, one of the sons of Olam, spoke up and said to Ezra, “We have trespassed against our <dn>Elohim</dn>, and have taken foreign women from the peoples of the land. And now there is expectancy in Yisra’ěl concerning this. [3] “Now then, let us make a covenant with our <dn>Elohim</dn> to put away <dn>את</dn> all these wives and <dn>את</dn> those who have been born to them, according to the counsel of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and of those who tremble at the command of our <dn>Elohim</dn>. And let it be done according to the Torah. [4] “Arise, for the matter is upon you, but we are with you. Be strong and act.” [5] And Ezra rose, and made the leaders of the priests, the Lěvites, and all Yisra’ěl, to swear to do according to this word. And they swore.

readings.title: The Assembly of the Exiles
readings.subtitle: The Ultimatum of the Ban for the Rebellious
readings.text: [Ezra 10:6] Then Ezra rose up from before the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and went into the room of Yehoḥanan son of Elyashiḇ. And he went there – he ate no bread and drank no water for he mourned because of the trespass of the exiles. [7] And they passed a call throughout Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim to all the sons of the exile, to gather at Yerushalayim, [8] and that whoever would not come within three days, according to the counsel of the leaders and elders, all his goods would be put under a ban, and himself separated from the assembly of the exiles.

readings.title: The Confession of Guilt
readings.subtitle: Separating from the Peoples of the Land
readings.text: [Ezra 10:9] Then all the men of Yehuḏah and Binyamin gathered at Yerushalayim within three days. It was the ninth new moon, on the twentieth of the new moon. And all the people sat in the open space of the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>, trembling because of the matter and because of showers of rain. [10] And Ezra the priest stood up and said to them, “You, you have trespassed and have taken <dn>את</dn> foreign women, adding to the guilt of Yisra’ěl. [11] “And now, make confession to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of your fathers, and do <dn>His</dn> desire, and separate yourselves from the peoples of the land, and from the foreign women.”

readings.title: The Execution of Justice
readings.subtitle: Examining the Breach of the Torah
readings.text: [Ezra 10:12] And all the assembly answered and said with a loud voice, “Right! It is upon us to do according to your word. [13] “But the people are many, and it is the season of showers of rain, and we are not able to stand outside. And the work not of one or two days, for we have greatly transgressed in this matter. [14] “Please, let the leaders of all the assembly stand. And let all those in our cities who have taken foreign women come at appointed times, together with the elders and judges of their cities, until the burning wrath of our <dn>Elohim</dn> is turned away from us in this matter.” [15] Only Yonathan son of Asah’ěl and Yaḥzeyah son of Tiqvah opposed this, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Lěvite gave them support. [16] Then the sons of the exile did so. And Ezra the priest, with certain heads of the fathers’ houses, were separated by the fathers’ houses, each of them by name. And they sat down on the first day of the tenth new moon to examine <dn>את</dn> the matter. [17] And they finished with <dn>את</dn> all the men who had taken foreign women by the first day of the first new moon.

readings.title: The Record of the Trespassers
readings.subtitle: The Census of Those Ensnared in Foreign Alliances
readings.text: [Ezra 10:18] And among the sons of the priests who had taken foreign women were found of the sons of Yěshua son of Yotsaḏaq, and his brothers: Ma‛asěyah, and Eli‛ezer, and Yariḇ, and Geḏalyah. [19] And they gave their hand in pledge to put away their wives. And being guilty, they presented a ram of the flock for their guilt. [20] And of the sons of Imměr: Ḥanani and Zeḇaḏyah; [21] and of the sons of Ḥarim: Ma‛asěyah, and Ěliyah, and Shemayah, and Yeḥi’ěl, and Uzziyah; [22] and of the sons of Pashḥur: Elyo‛ěynai, Ma‛asěyah, Yishma‛ěl, Nethan’ěl, Yozaḇaḏ, and El‛asah. [23] And of the Lěvites: Yozaḇaḏ, Shim‛i, Qělayah – he is Qelita – Pethaḥyah, Yehuḏah, and Eli‛ezer. [24] And of the singers: Elyashiḇ. And of the gatekeepers: Shallum, and Telem, and Uri. [25] And of Yisra’ěl of the sons of Parosh: Ramyah, and Yizziyah, and Malkiyah, and Miyamin, and El‛azar, and Malkiyah, and Benayah; [26] and of the sons of Ěylam: Mattanyah, Zeḵaryah, and Yeḥi’ěl, and Aḇdi, and Yerěmoth, and Ěliyah; [27] and of the sons of Zattu: Elyo‛ěynai, Elyashiḇ, Mattanyah, and Yerěmoth, and Zaḇaḏ, and Aziza; [28] and of the sons of Běḇai: Yehoḥanan, Ḥananyah, Zabbai, and Athlai; [29] and of the sons of Bani: Meshullam, Malluḵ, and Aḏayah, Yashuḇ, and She’al, Ramoth; [30] and of the sons of Paḥath-Mo’aḇ: Aḏna, and Kelal, Benayah, Ma‛asěyah, Mattanyah, Betsal’ěl, and Binnui, and Menashsheh; [31] and of the sons of Ḥarim: Eli‛ezer, Yishshiyah, Malkiyah, Shemayah, Shim‛on, [32] Binyamin, Malluḵ, and Shemaryah; [33] of the sons of Ḥashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zaḇaḏ, Eliphelet, Yerěmai, Menashsheh, and Shim‛i; [34] of the sons of Bani: Ma‛aḏai, Amram, and U’ěl, [35] Benayah, Běḏeyah, Keluhu, [36] Wanyah, Merěmoth, Elyashiḇ, [37] Mattanyah, Mattenai, and Ya‛asu, [38] and Bani, and Binnui, Shim‛i, [39] and Shelemyah, and Nathan, and Aḏayah, [40] Maḵnaḏeḇai, Shashai, Sharai, [41] Azar’ěl, and Shelemyahu, Shemaryah, [42] Shallum, Amaryah, and Yosěph; [43] of the sons of Neḇo: Ye‛i’ěl, Mattithyah, Zaḇaḏ, Zeḇina, Yaddu, and Yo’ěl, Benayah. [44] All these had taken foreign women, and some of them had women who had borne children.

readings.title: The Ruin of the Gates
readings.subtitle: Nehemyah Hears of the Broken Defenses
readings.text: [Nehemiah 1:1] The words of Neḥemyah son of Ḥaḵalyah. And it came to be in the new moon of Kislěv, in the twentieth year, as I was in the citadel of Shushan, [2] that Ḥanani, one of my brothers, came with men from Yehuḏah. And I asked them concerning <dn>את</dn> the Yehuḏim who had escaped, who had survived the captivity, and concerning <dn>את</dn> Yerushalayim. [3] And they said to me, “The remnant who are left of the captivity in the province are there in great evil and reproach. And the wall of Yerushalayim is broken down, and its gates are burned with fire.” [4] And it came to be, when I heard these words, that I sat down and wept, and mourned for many days. And I was fasting and praying before the <dn>Elohim</dn> of the heavens,

readings.title: The Prayer of Confession
readings.subtitle: Acknowledging the Breach of the Torah and Right-Rulings
readings.text: [Nehemiah 1:5] and I said, “I pray, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of the heavens, O great and awesome <dn>Ěl</dn>, guarding the covenant and loving-commitment with those who love You, and with those guarding Your commands, [6] please let Your ear be attentive and Your eyes open, to hear <dn>את</dn> the prayer of Your servant which I am praying before You now, day and night, for the children of Yisra’ěl Your servants, and confess <dn>את</dn> the sins of the children of Yisra’ěl which we have sinned against You. Both my father’s house and I have sinned. [7] “We have acted very corruptly against You, and have not guarded <dn>את</dn> the commands, nor <dn>את</dn> the laws, nor <dn>את</dn> the right-rulings which You commanded Your servant Mosheh.

readings.title: The Promise of the Gathering
readings.subtitle: Leaning on the Covenantal Guarantee of the Right Arm
readings.text: [Nehemiah 1:8] “Please remember <dn>את</dn> the word that You commanded <dn>את</dn> Your servant Mosheh, saying, <dq>‘If you trespass, <dn>I</dn> shall scatter you among the peoples,</dq> [9] <dq>but if you shall turn back to <dn>Me</dn>, and guard <dn>My</dn> commands and do them, though you were cast out to the end of the heavens, <dn>I</dn> shall gather them from there, and bring them to the place which <dn>I</dn> have chosen, to make <dn>My</dn> Name dwell there.’</dq> [10] “And they are Your servants and Your people, whom You have ransomed by Your great power, and by Your strong hand. [11] “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, I pray, please let Your ear be attentive to the prayer of Your servant, and to the prayer of Your servants who delight to fear Your Name. And let Your servant prosper this day, I pray, and grant him <dn>את</dn> compassion in the presence of this man.” For I was cupbearer to the sovereign.

readings.title: The Petition to the Sovereign
readings.subtitle: Seeking Jurisdiction to Rebuild the Foundations
readings.text: [Nehemiah 2:1] And it came to be in the new moon of Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaḥshashta the sovereign, when wine was before him, that I took <dn>את</dn> the wine and gave it to the sovereign. And I had never been sad in his presence. [2] And the sovereign said to me, “Why is your face sad, since you are not sick? This is none else but sorrow of heart.” Then I was very much afraid, [3] and said to the sovereign, “Let the sovereign live forever! Why should my face not be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers’ burial-sites, lies waste, and its gates are burned with fire?” [4] And the sovereign said to me, “What are you asking for?” Then I prayed to the <dn>Elohim</dn> of the heavens, [5] and said to the sovereign, “If it seems good to the sovereign, and if your servant is pleasing before you, I ask that you send me to Yehuḏah, to the city of my fathers’ burial-sites, so that I build it.”

readings.title: The Decrees of Provision
readings.subtitle: Securing the Timber and Letters for the Restoration
readings.text: [Nehemiah 2:6] And the sovereign, with the sovereigness sitting beside him, said to me, “How long would your journey take? And when do you return?” So it seemed good before the sovereign to send me. And I set him a time. [7] And I said to the sovereign, “If it seems good to the sovereign, let letters be given to me for the governors beyond the River, that they should let me to pass through till I come to Yehuḏah, [8] and a letter to Asaph the keeper of the sovereign’s forest, that he should give me timber to make beams for the gates of the palace that belongs to the House, and for the city wall, and for the house I would enter.” And the sovereign gave them to me according to the good hand of my <dn>Elohim</dn> upon me.

readings.title: The Arrival in Yehuḏah
readings.subtitle: The Adversary's Proxies Disturbed by the Restorative Mission
readings.text: [Nehemiah 2:9] Then I came to the governors beyond the River, and gave to them <dn>את</dn> the letters of the sovereign. Now the sovereign had sent commanders of the army and horsemen with me. [10] And Sanballat the Ḥoronite and Toḇiyah the Ammonite official heard of it, and to them it was evil, a great evil that a man had come to seek good for the children of Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: The Midnight Survey
readings.subtitle: Assessing the Structural Damage of the City
readings.text: [Nehemiah 2:11] Then I came to Yerushalayim and was there three days. [12] And I rose up in the night, I and a few men with me, but informed no one <dn>את</dn> what my <dn>Elohim</dn> had put in my heart to do at Yerushalayim, nor was there any beast with me, except the beast on which I rode. [13] And I went out by night through the Valley Gate to the Jackals’ Fountain and the Dung Gate, and examined <dn>את</dn> the walls of Yerushalayim which were broken down and its gates which were burned with fire. [14] And I went on to the Fountain Gate and to the Sovereign’s Pool, but there was no room for the beast that was under me to pass. [15] And I went up in the night by the wadi, and examined <dn>את</dn> the wall, and turned back, and entered by the Valley Gate, and returned. [16] And the deputy rulers did not know where I had gone nor what I had done. Nor had I yet informed the Yehuḏim, or the priests, or the nobles, or the deputy rulers, or the others who did the work.

readings.title: The Call to Rebuild
readings.subtitle: Making the Hands Strong for the Work of Tov
readings.text: [Nehemiah 2:17] Then I said to them, “You see <dn>את</dn> the evil which we are in, how Yerushalayim lies waste, and its gates are burned with fire. Come and let us build <dn>את</dn> the wall of Yerushalayim, and let us no longer be a reproach.” [18] And I informed them of <dn>את</dn> the hand of my <dn>Elohim</dn> which had been good upon me, and also of <dn>את</dn> the sovereign’s words he had spoken to me. And they said, “Let us rise up and we shall build.” So they made their hands strong for good.

readings.title: The Rejection of the Mockers
readings.subtitle: Denying the Adversary Any Portion in Yerushalayim
readings.text: [Nehemiah 2:19] But when Sanballat the Ḥoronite heard, and Toḇiyah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Araḇ, they mocked us and despised us, and said, “What is this you are doing? Are you rebelling against the sovereign?” [20] And I answered them, and said to them, “The <dn>Elohim</dn> of the heavens, <dn>He</dn> shall bless us and let us, <dn>His</dn> servants, rise and build, but you have no portion or right or remembrance in Yerushalayim.”
